investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-03T18:23:24–18:23:57Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable. Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, causing a complete contract violation for all three checks.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB endpoint that backs POST /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api runtime at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls POST /api/agents, which proxies to this ELB; the gateway returned a 502 bad_gateway with the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" before any agent lifecycle could begin. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure localized to the swarm provisioning gateway in us-east-2; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

The ELB target group behind the swarm gateway lost all healthy instances (e.g., due to a deployment, scaling event, or health-check failure), causing the load balancer to return 502 with no upstream to forward to

A misconfiguration or credential/routing change in the production-api layer caused it to route agent provisioning requests to an incorrect or decommissioned ELB endpoint — less likely given the error message explicitly names the ELB URL and the error code is bad_gateway rather than not_found or unauthorized

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the GitHub Actions workflow run history shows a successful publish within the last 300 minutes relative to the eval run time (2026-09-03T18:24:00Z), the staleness would be caused by a caching or CDN layer rather than a missed workflow run.

If fetching status.json directly returns a generatedAt timestamp within 300 minutes of the eval run time, the snapshotAgeMinutes value computed by the runner may be incorrect (e.g., a timezone or clock skew bug in statusSnapshotEvidence), which would shift the root cause to the eval runner rather than the workflow.

If the check passes on an immediate re-run with snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300, the workflow ran successfully shortly after the eval and the failure was a transient timing gap rather than a sustained workflow outage.

If the registry staleAfterMinutes=360 (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) is the intended freshness gate and the contract max:300 is a misconfiguration, the root cause would be a contract/registry mismatch rather than a workflow failure.
